key_insight: Dissipative spin hydrodynamics couples spin and orbital angular momentum, with simulations indicating that spin polarization approaches thermal vorticity.
engineering_relevance: Consistent spin–momentum coupling can improve continuum modeling of spin-polarized fluids undergoing relativistic expansion.
method: Extend perfect spin hydrodynamics with antisymmetric energy–momentum contributions.
Compare Navier–Stokes and Israel–Stewart descriptions of spin dissipation.
Simulate longitudinal Bjorken and cylindrically symmetric boost-invariant expansions.
evidence_signal: Numerical results across varied spin kinetic coefficients and relaxation times show polarization approaching thermal vorticity, with Israel–Stewart evolution first approaching the Navier–Stokes regime.
watch_item: Kinetic coefficients and relaxation times remain unspecified a priori, while the Navier–Stokes formulation can introduce higher-than-first-order derivatives that disrupt the equation structure.
paper_title: Novel hydrodynamic features in dissipative spin-polarized fluids
